body:
New article: none yet, this is a new page.

**Source:** [WordPress 7.2 Source of Truth](https://wordpress-source-of-truth.space.fast/7-2/), section 03 "Editor enhancements", item "Clearer error screens"
**Background:** [Defensive data design](https://make.wordpress.org/core/2026/08/04/defensive-data-design/) (Make Core, August 4, 2026)
**Planning issue:** #2567 has no line for this yet.
**Related:** the [Block Error: Unexpected or Invalid Content](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/block-error-unexpected-or-invalid-content/) article covers errors in a single block. Link the two pages to each other.

## Pages to update

- [ ] **New article**, for example "When the editor shows an error". It explains what the editor's error messages mean and what to do next.
- [ ] **[Block Error: Unexpected or Invalid Content](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/block-error-unexpected-or-invalid-content/)**: add a short line pointing to the new article, for when the whole editor stops working rather than one block. Last updated June 22, 2026.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** When the editor runs into a problem, it now says what happened in plainer words and makes it easier to get help. Save failure messages explain what happened to your changes, and a **Show details** button reveals the server's message with a button to copy it. If the editor crashes, **Copy error** now copies a full report you can paste into a support forum post or a bug report. The Site Editor no longer goes blank when part of it fails, and shows the error screen instead.

- [ ] **Clearer save failure messages.** When saving, publishing or scheduling fails, the message now says which one failed. When an autosave fails, it explains that your changes are kept in your browser and that WordPress will try again, or you can save by hand. The server's raw error text is no longer added to the end of the message.
  [Editor: clarify save failure notices (#76470)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/76470)
  *Suggested action:* a section in the new article, for example "If saving fails", listing the messages and what to do.

- [ ] **Show details and copy the error.** Save failure messages now have a **Show details** button that reveals the server's explanation. A **Copy error** button copies the message and the details, so you can paste them into a search, a forum post or a message to your host.
  [Editor: add copy option for save failures & a "show/hide details" button (#82496)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82496)
  *Suggested action:* part of the same section, with a tip to include the copied text when asking for help.

- [ ] **A more useful Copy error report when the editor crashes.** On the "The editor has encountered an unexpected error" screen, **Copy error** now copies a report with the error message, where in the editor it happened and which browser you use. When `SCRIPT_DEBUG` is turned on, the screen also shows these details in a panel you can open.
  [Editor: Surface debugging details in the ErrorBoundary (#81642)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81642)
  *Suggested action:* a section in the new article, for example "If the editor stops working". Keep the `SCRIPT_DEBUG` part to one sentence with a link to the debugging docs, since it's for developers.

- [ ] **No blank Site Editor.** If part of the Site Editor fails, it now shows the error screen instead of going completely blank, so you get a message and the **Copy error** button.
  [Site Editor: Add a root error boundary to prevent a blank screen (#82486)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82486), core ticket [Trac #66047](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/66047)
  *Suggested action:* one sentence in the same section, so Site Editor users know the screen applies to them too.

- [ ] **What to do next.** Add short, plain steps for both cases: copy the error, try again, check plugins and the theme, and where to ask for help (the [support forums](https://wordpress.org/support/forums/)). Link to [Common WordPress errors](https://developer.wordpress.org/advanced-administration/wordpress/common-errors/) for server-side problems rather than repeating them.

### Check on the RC build before writing

These details came from the PRs and the Source of Truth, and the UI may have changed since. Please confirm them on the latest 7.2 release candidate ([Playground](https://playground.wordpress.net/release)):

- [ ] The exact wording of the save failure messages, including the autosave one.
- [ ] The labels of **Show details**, **Copy error** and the "Copied" confirmation.
- [ ] The wording on the editor error screen and which buttons it shows (for example **Copy error** and **Copy post text**).
- [ ] A way to trigger each message for screenshots. Turning off your network connection while saving should show a save failure message. The crash screen may only be reachable with a test plugin, so a recreated screenshot or one from the PRs may be the practical option.

### Not in 7.2, don't document

- The `editor.ErrorBoundary.errorLogged` action and the deprecated `__unstableHTML` notice option. They're for developers.
- The same blank screen gap in other admin screens built on the new boot package. The PR notes it needs its own follow-up.

## Screenshots and media

- **Needed:** a save failure message with **Show details** opened, and the editor error screen with **Copy error**.
- **Annotations would help:** point to **Show details** and **Copy error**.
- **Reusable from PRs** (check they match the RC build before using): #81642 has screenshots of the error screen in the post editor and the Site Editor, #82486 has two screenshots, and #76470 has one.
- The Source of Truth authors ask that their text isn't copied. Paraphrase rather than paste.

## General
- [ ] Make sure all screenshots are relevant to the latest version
- [ ] Add ALT tags for the images
- [ ] Make sure the headings are in sentence case
- [ ] Add a changelog at the end of the new article, and update the changelog of the Block Error article
- [ ] Publish the new article and the Block Error update on release day (December 8, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC), so they don't describe 7.2 before it ships. Use **Save for later** for the Block Error update.

<details>
<summary>Directions (click to open)</summary>

- Compare existing screenshots (on the article link) to the actual interface in the latest WordPress version.
- Ensure you have the appropriate WordPress version and that new screenshots cover the same page area as the existing one.
- If something is different in the latest version, make a new screenshot.
- Upload new screenshots directly to the article.
- Request review by editing your comment to say "Ready for 1st Review".

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes (click to open)</summary>

1. You can set WordPress install in one click by visiting https://playground.wordpress.net/ or use InstaWP sandbox https://app.instawp.io/onboard
2. We are not adding detailed updates for the Block settings - Typography, Color, Layout, Dimension and Border and for the More Options setting in the block toolbar. Pls mention the settings included for the block and link to the detailed settings pages instead.
3. Some of the PRs have great videos that can be added to the article.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Automation (click to open)</summary>

If you want, you can assign yourself to the issue and change the label for review by posting specific keywords in a comment:
- Assign yourself: `/assign`
- Request review: `/review`

Read about our repo's automatisation [here](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/handbook/github-repository-and-projects/documentation-issue-tracker/#label-issues).

</details>

AI assistance: Yes. Tool: Claude. Used for: comparing the Source of Truth and the Gutenberg PRs against existing HelpHub articles on editor errors, and drafting this issue. Reviewed by @chekle before posting.

title: Planning for 7.2
body:
# WordPress 7.2 Docs Checklist

**Goal:** A plan to have 7.2 docs ready by [the planned December 8 release date](https://make.wordpress.org/core/7-2/). I wanted to get at least a draft up of what needs to be done. We can validate and iterate as needed.

Regarding timing, I'm worried about missing December 8 with folks being busy with holidays and life. Hoping to get ahead where we can. RC1 releases today, so while there may be some changes still, we should at least be able to start planning, and if some tasks should be saved for last, we can identify those.

Here are the overall steps, and I've included a list of claude-found potential issues-to-create below. What else needs to be done? And what can be dialed in & simplified? What must be prioritized?

- [ ] Verify which issues need to be created (see below)
- [ ] Create issues
- [ ] Start drafting what we can now.
- [ ] Get a plan ready with dates and assignments
- [ ] Figure out how to handle Design Tools update (there are a lot)
- [ ] Decide how to handle screenshots, and handle them

## Issues to create

### Block and site editor

## Issue Description
The **Removing Meta Boxes** section says: "The default `add_meta_box()` calls are made from `wp-includes/edit-form-advanced.php`." That file does not exist. The edit screen is `wp-admin/edit-form-advanced.php`, and it does not call `add_meta_box()` directly either. It calls `register_and_do_post_meta_boxes()` (since WordPress 5.0), and the default `add_meta_box()` calls live in that function in `wp-admin/includes/meta-boxes.php`.

This was also reported in WordPress/developer-plugins-handbook#58.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/metadata/custom-meta-boxes/

## Section of Page with the issue
https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/metadata/custom-meta-boxes/#removing-meta-boxes

## Why is this a problem?
The sentence tells developers where to look up the IDs and contexts they must pass to `remove_meta_box()`. The path points to a file that does not exist, so they cannot find the parameters.

## Suggested Fix
"…calls are made from `wp-includes/edit-form-advanced.php`." → "…calls are made from [`register_and_do_post_meta_boxes()`](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/register_and_do_post_meta_boxes/) in `wp-admin/includes/meta-boxes.php`."

I have a PR ready for developer-plugins-handbook.

Article to update: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/settings-permalinks-screen/

**Source:** [WordPress 7.2 Source of Truth](https://wordpress-source-of-truth.space.fast/7-2/), section 04 "Admin / Workflow updates", item "Random content redirects"
**Core ticket:** [Trac #64498](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/64498) (Add core support for random content redirects). Follow-ups fixed for 7.2: [Trac #66625](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/66625) (cache and noindex headers) and [Trac #66654](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/66654) (performance on large sites).
**Dev note:** [Your Content Is Going To Get More Random!](https://make.wordpress.org/core/2026/11/05/your-content-is-going-to-get-more-random/) (Make Core, November 5, 2026)
**Planning issue:** #2567 (the "Settings Permalinks screen: Random base" and "Random base" lines)

## Pages to update

- [ ] **[Settings Permalinks screen](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/settings-permalinks-screen/)**: add **Random base** to the **Optional** section, next to **Category base** and **Tag base**. Last updated June 8, 2024, so check the rest of the page against 7.2 too.
- [ ] **[Customize permalinks](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/customize-permalinks/)**: a short section, for example "Random content links", with the URL patterns below. It already has a **Category base and Tag base** section, so the new section fits after it. Last updated June 28, 2025.

**Note, no action needed in this issue:** #2567 also notes that the `register_post_type()` reference has no mention of the new `randomable` argument. That's developer documentation (DevHub), not HelpHub, so it's out of scope here.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** WordPress 7.2 adds links that send visitors to a random published post. Visiting `/random/` on a site with pretty permalinks opens a random post, and the same works within a category, tag, author or post type. It's on by default. Site owners can change the `random` part of the address in **Settings > Permalinks**, for example to `shuffle`.

- [ ] **Random content links.** With pretty permalinks turned on, these addresses send visitors to a random published post:
  - `/random/` for any post.
  - `/random/category/news/` for a post in the News category. Tags work the same way, for example `/random/tag/recipes/`.
  - `/random/author/username/` for a post by that author.
  - `/random/post-type-slug/` for a custom post type that has an archive, if it allows it.

  Pages and media files aren't included. You can add one of these addresses to a menu as a custom link, for example a "Random post" link in the header.
  [Trac #64498](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/64498), [r64402](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/changeset/64402)
  *Suggested action:* the new section in Customize permalinks. Mention that it needs pretty permalinks (it doesn't work with **Plain**).

- [ ] **Random base setting.** **Settings > Permalinks** has a new **Random base** field under **Optional**. It changes the `random` part of the address. Leave it blank to use the default. Sites in other languages get a translated default.
  *Sections affected:* **Optional** in Settings Permalinks screen (one entry, in the same style as **Category base** and **Tag base**).

- [ ] **Pages named "random" come first.** If a page already uses the slug `random`, visitors still see that page. To use random links on such a site, change the **Random base**, for example to `shuffle`.
  *Suggested action:* one sentence with the **Random base** entry.

- [ ] **Version details.** Add a changelog entry to each updated page.

### Check on the RC build before writing

**Where the discussion is:** the [dev note comments](https://make.wordpress.org/core/2026/11/05/your-content-is-going-to-get-more-random/#comments) (over 100, mostly asking for the feature to be opt-in or use `/?random`) and [Trac #64498](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/64498). As of November 20, the last dev note comment was on November 16, the ticket is closed, and no change to the shipped behavior has been announced. If a follow-up ticket or post appears, link it here.

Please confirm these on the latest 7.2 release candidate ([Playground](https://playground.wordpress.net/release)) before writing:

- [ ] That `/random/` still works as described, and whether `/?random` also works. A comment on the dev note suggested using `?random` at the root instead of a path, so check which one shipped.
- [ ] The exact label of the **Random base** field and where it sits on **Settings > Permalinks**.
- [ ] Which address patterns work (category, tag, author, post type), and that pages and media aren't included.
- [ ] That the feature is still on by default. If it changed to off by default or got a setting to turn it on, document that instead.

### Not in 7.2, don't document

- Turning the feature off with the `wp_enable_random_content_redirect` filter, the `randomable` argument for post types, and `wp_is_random_content_query()`. They're for developers (the dev note and Field Guide). If the RC build shows the **Random base** field is hidden, mention only that a plugin or theme can turn the feature off.
- The cache and noindex headers, and the performance work for large sites. Nothing changes for users.

## Screenshots and media

- **Needed:** the **Optional** section of **Settings > Permalinks** showing the new **Random base** field.
- **Annotations would help:** point to the **Random base** field.
- No screenshots are available from the Source of Truth, Trac or the dev note.
- The Source of Truth authors ask that their text isn't copied. Paraphrase rather than paste.

body:
Article to update: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/query-loop-block/ (plus 11 more block articles, listed below)

**Source:** [WordPress 7.2 Source of Truth](https://wordpress-source-of-truth.space.fast/7-2/), section 02 "Improved Blocks and Block handling", item "General quality of life improvements"
**Planning issue:** #2567 (the Query Loop, Columns, Button, Cover and Media & Text, and List lines)
**Related:** the Work with blocks article is also updated by #2558 and the writing improvements issue. Coordinate so the updates don't overwrite each other.

## Pages to update

Each line below is a separate, small change to one article. Add a sentence or two, link to the settings overview pages if needed, and update a screenshot where the line says so. Work on one block at a time.

- [ ] **[Query Loop block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/query-loop-block/)**: the taxonomy filters (Categories, Tags and others) now list the existing terms when you open them, so you can pick from a list instead of typing from memory. Selected terms show as chips you can remove, and a term can't be both included and excluded. The **Keyword** filter is now called **Search terms** and has help text.
  [Query Loop: list taxonomy terms so they can be browsed, not recalled (#82583)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82583), [Query Loop: Rename the "Keyword" filter to "Search terms" and add help text (#82387)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82387)
  *Sections affected:* **Block settings > Settings** (the filters). Last updated September 5, 2026.
- [ ] **[Columns block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/columns-block/)**: the column count slider and its warning above six columns are gone from the block settings. You add and remove columns with the usual insert and delete actions, for example the plus button. Columns can also be transformed into a Row.
  [Columns: Remove the column count slider (#83262)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83262), [Add transform to Row for Columns block (#81802)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81802)
  *Sections affected:* **Adding and removing columns**, **Block settings > Settings tabs** and **Block toolbar > Transform to**. Last updated August 25, 2026.
- [ ] **[Buttons block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/buttons-block/)**: the link popover no longer opens every time you select a button that has a link. It opens only when you select **Link** in the toolbar, so you can edit the button text without it getting in the way.
  [Button: Only open the link popover on explicit user action (#30166)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/30166)
  *Sections affected:* **Block toolbar > For an individual button**. Last updated September 1, 2026.
- [ ] **[Cover block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/cover-block/)**: a new **Media** section in the block settings sidebar lets you add or replace the background, including the featured image, even when the Cover has no media yet. In the editor, a background video doesn't autoplay when your device is set to reduce motion, and embedded background videos (such as YouTube) don't autoplay for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
  [Cover Block: Add a Media section to the block inspector panel (#82751)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82751), [Video, Cover: Don't autoplay in the editor when reduced motion is preferred (#83337)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83337), [Cover: Don't autoplay embedded background videos when reduced motion is preferred (#83452)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83452)
  *Sections affected:* **Block settings > Settings** (new Media section) and the background video part of **Add media / Replace**. Last updated August 19, 2026.
- [ ] **[Media & Text block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/media-text-block/)**: a new **Media** section in the block settings sidebar, and an **Add media** button in the toolbar when the block has no media yet. Before, the toolbar only showed **Replace** once media was set.

**Summary:** In WordPress 7.1, the block editor started creating image sizes in your browser instead of on the server. In 7.2, uploads from the Media Library, the Add New Media File screen and the media window (for example the **Media Library** button in an Image block or the featured image panel) work the same way in supported browsers. - [ ] **Images are processed in the browser on more screens.** In a supported browser, uploading an image in the Media Library grid, on the Add New Media File screen or in the media window creates the image sizes in the browser. This makes large uploads less likely to time out or run out of memory on the server. The upload screens look the same as before, with the same progress bars and messages. - [ ] **Animated GIF and WebP images stay animated.** When an animated GIF or WebP is processed in the browser, its smaller sizes, including cropped ones such as the thumbnail, keep the animation.

If you didn't expect it, you can revoke it. On sites without HTTPS, the notice in the Application Passwords section now says exactly which environment type you need to set to use them.

- [ ] **Email when an application password is created.** When an application password is added to a user's account, by the user or by an administrator, WordPress sends that user an email. It names the application password and the site, and tells the user what to do if they didn't expect it. An application password can act on the user's behalf through the REST API, so this helps people spot access they didn't give.

body:
Article to update: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/work-with-blocks/

**Source:** [WordPress 7.2 Source of Truth](https://wordpress-source-of-truth.space.fast/7-2/), section 03 "Editor enhancements", item "Fewer paper cuts while writing"
**Tracking issue:** [Block Editor Paper Cuts (gutenberg#81453)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/81453). Only the ticked items shipped in 7.2.
**Planning issue:** #2567 (the "Adding a new block" and "Work with Blocks: non-breaking spaces" lines)
**Related:** the 7.2 issue "Work with blocks: Top toolbar is now under Options > Appearance" (#2558) also updates the Work with blocks article. Coordinate so the two updates don't overwrite each other.

## Pages to update

- [ ] **[Work with blocks](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/work-with-blocks/)**: the main update (details below). Last changed November 19, 2026.
- [ ] **[Adding a new block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/adding-a-new-block/)**: the inserter next to the parent selector, and the in-between inserter on wrapped rows. Last updated June 22, 2026.
- [ ] **[Moving blocks](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/moving-blocks/)**: dragging several selected blocks. Last updated September 2, 2026.
- [ ] **[Use keyboard shortcuts (Block Editor)](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/keyboard-shortcuts-block-editor/)**: Escape and Enter to leave and return to the canvas. Last updated November 1, 2026.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** WordPress 7.2 fixes a set of small annoyances while writing. You can bold or link text that runs across several blocks, select several blocks on a phone or tablet, and drag a selection of blocks by grabbing any of them. Escape now takes you out of the editing area and Enter takes you back. You can add a block from the parent selector in the toolbar, and the editor marks non-breaking spaces so you can find and replace them.

- [ ] **Formatting across blocks.** If you select text that starts in one block and ends in another, the formatting buttons in the block toolbar and their shortcuts (bold, italic, link and the others) now apply to the whole selection.
  [Allow rich text formatting across blocks (#58913)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/58913)
  *Sections affected:* **Selecting multiple blocks** in Work with blocks (add a sentence after the list of ways to select).

- [ ] **Selecting multiple blocks on mobile.** You can now select several blocks in a mobile browser, for example on an iPhone or iPad.
  [Re-enable editableRoot for multi-selection on mobile web (#81542)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81542)
  *Sections affected:* **Selecting multiple blocks** in Work with blocks. One sentence is enough.

- [ ] **Drag a selection from anywhere inside it.** When several blocks are selected, you can drag them by pressing anywhere on the selection, not only on the drag handle in the toolbar.
  [Drag a multi-selection (#81602)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81602)
  *Sections affected:* **Using the drag & drop** in Moving blocks, and optionally **Selecting multiple blocks** in Work with blocks (it lists moving as a reason to select several blocks).

- [ ] **Escape leaves the canvas, Enter goes back in.** Pressing Escape while editing moves focus out of the editing area, so you can reach the toolbar and the sidebar with Tab. Pressing Enter returns you to the content. Screen reader users may need to press Escape twice, because the first press switches the screen reader out of focus mode.
  [Tab trap escape hatch: leave/enter the canvas with Escape/Enter (#82314)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82314)
  *Sections affected:* **Global shortcuts** in the keyboard shortcuts article (add a row). Check whether **Clear selection: Escape** in **Selection shortcuts** is still accurate.

- [ ] **Add a block from the parent selector.** When a block inside another block is selected (for example an image in a Gallery), an inserter button next to the parent selector in the block toolbar adds a new block after it.
  [Block editor: add an inserter to the parent selector (#81532)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81532)
  *Sections affected:* **How to add blocks within nested blocks** in Adding a new block.

- [ ] **In-between inserter on wrapped rows.** When blocks in a row wrap onto a second line, for example buttons in a Buttons block, hovering between two blocks on the second line now shows the inserter.
  [Block Editor: Show the in-between inserter on wrapped lines (#83276)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83276)
  *Sections affected:* **Using the Block inserter icon in between blocks** in Adding a new block. Likely one sentence.

- [ ] **Non-breaking spaces are marked.** In the selected block, non-breaking spaces show as a small red dot. When the cursor is next to one, or your selection includes one, a toolbar button replaces them with regular spaces. This helps when pasted text wraps in odd places.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** The block toolbar button that opens the media editor is now called **Edit image**, because the editor does more than crop. If you've edited an image, you can now go back to the original from the editor's **More options** menu. When you save a post, images in it that aren't attached to any post get attached to it.

- [ ] **The Crop button is now Edit image.** In the Image, Cover and Site Logo blocks, the toolbar button that opens the media editor was **Crop** (or **Crop background image** in the Cover block). It's now **Edit image** in all three.
  [Rename the media editor toolbar button to 'Edit image' (#81705)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81705)
  *Sections affected:* the **Crop** heading and its first sentence ("Use the Crop button...") in all three articles. Consider renaming the heading to **Edit image**.

- [ ] **Restore the original image.** When you open an image you've already edited, the media editor's **More options** menu has a **Restore original image** option. It loads the original, uncropped image in the editor. What happens next depends on what you do:
  - Save without other changes: the block uses the original image again, and no new image is created.
  - Crop again, then save: a new image is created from the original, not from the earlier crop.
  - Cancel: your restore is discarded.

  The option doesn't show for images that have never been edited. The keyboard shortcuts also moved into the **More options** menu.
  [Media editor: restore original image in modal (#81805)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81805), which relies on [Media: track the original attachment id for edited images (#81803)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81803)

- [ ] **Optional: images attached to the post on save.** When you save or publish a post, images in Image and Gallery blocks that aren't attached to another post are attached to it. ## Pages to update

- [ ] **[Navigation block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/navigation-block/)**: the main update (details below). Last updated October 8, 2026.
- [ ] **[Custom Link block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/custom-link-block/)**: the block is now called Navigation Link, and Custom Link is its default variation. Last updated May 25, 2026.
- [ ] **[Site Editor navigation](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/site-editor-navigation/)**: link editing in the sidebar and the inserter for empty menus. The intro still talks about WordPress 6.3.
- [ ] **[Page List block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/page-list-block/)**: **Edit** is now **Detach**, with a confirmation dialog. Last updated July 23, 2026.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** Adding a link to a menu is now one search. The search box finds pages, posts, categories, tags and media together, shows what type each result is, and also lists blocks such as Home Link. You can change a link's type without deleting it. The block behind each menu link is now called Navigation Link, with Custom Link as its default variation. ## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** Any gallery can now be sorted with an **Order by** setting, not only galleries that use attached images. **Randomize order** becomes one of the **Order by** options. A new Grid variation lets you resize individual images, for example to make one image span two columns. On phones, swiping between images in the lightbox is now animated, so visitors can tell they can swipe.

- [ ] **Order by for all galleries.** Galleries you build by hand get the same **Order by** setting as galleries that use attached images. Choosing an option sorts the images once, and you can still drag them into a different order afterwards. A gallery you've arranged by hand shows **Custom**. **Random** is now one of the **Order by** options, so the separate **Randomize order** setting is gone. The sorting controls for both kinds of gallery now sit together in the **Settings** tab, and **Crop images to fit** moved to just below **Aspect ratio**. Images that can't be sorted, such as external images, go to the end of the gallery.
  [Gallery: Add Order By controls for static gallery, consolidate controls in settings sidebar (#83438)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83438)
  *Sections affected:* **Settings tab** (replace **Randomize order** with **Order by**, and update the order of the settings), **Move images** (mention that you can still reorder by hand after sorting), and **Use attached images**.

- [ ] **Grid variation.** The Gallery block now has two variations: the default layout and **Grid**. In the Grid variation you can resize individual images so they span more columns or rows. You switch between the two in the block settings sidebar, and your layout settings are kept if you switch back. In a gallery that uses attached images, the images can't be resized individually.
  [Try adding a Grid block variation to Gallery (#81909)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81909)
  *Suggested action:* add a short section, for example "Use the Grid layout", near **Block settings**. Link to the [Grid block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/grid-block/) article for how resizing grid items works rather than repeating it. Keep it separate from **Transform to > Grid**, which still converts the gallery into a Grid block of Image blocks.

- [ ] **Animated swiping in the lightbox.** When a gallery is set to **Enlarge on click**, swiping between images on a phone is now animated.
  [Gallery: Improve mobile lightbox with animated swiping (#79114)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/79114)
  *Sections affected:* **Link > Enlarge on click**. One sentence is enough, for example "On phones, visitors can swipe between images."

- [ ] **Use attached images and Detach wording.** The button is now **Use attached images**, with a short description above it ([#82617](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82617)). **Planning issue:** #2567 (the "88 blocks with new design tools" list)
**Related:** the per-block articles are covered in the design tools block batches (B1 to B6). Global Styles changes and responsive styles are covered separately.

## Pages to update

- [ ] **[Typography Settings overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/typography-settings-overview/)**
  - **Line indent:** the article says it works "on a paragraph block". It now also works on Heading ([#83615](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83615)), Post Author Biography ([#83614](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83614)) and Poetry ([#83962](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83962)).
  - **Columns:** now also on Group ([#83425](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83425)), Post Author Biography ([#83424](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83424)), Terms List ([#83432](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83432)) and Poetry ([#83962](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83962)).
  - **Fit text:** now also on Post Title ([#83036](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83036)), Site Title ([#82074](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82074)), Site Tagline ([#83034](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83034)) and Poetry ([#83980](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83980)).
  - Typography controls are new on Tabs, Tab Panel and Tab Panels ([#83431](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83431), [#83426](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83426), [#83428](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83428)), line height on Accordion Heading ([#83958](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83958)) and font family on Comments Form ([#83967](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83967)).
  - Text align is new on Content ([#83427](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83427)) and Table of Contents ([#83430](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83430)), and List gets block alignment ([#68002](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/68002)).

- [ ] **[Colors Settings overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/colors-settings-overview/)**
  - **Link, heading and button colors** (the **Elements** options) are now on many more blocks: Accordion, Accordion Item, Accordion Panel, Tabs, Tab Panel, Tab Panels, Quote, Details, Post Template, Comments, Comment Content, Media & Text, Content, Comments Form and No Results. Audio and Preformatted get link color, and Tag Cloud gets background and link color. PRs: [#83373](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83373), [#83371](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83371), [#83374](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83374), [#83390](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83390), [#83389](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83389), [#83388](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83388), [#83983](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83983), [#83381](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83381), [#83384](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83384), [#83378](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83378), [#83376](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83376), [#83380](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83380), [#83379](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83379), [#83377](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83377), [#83382](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83382), [#83375](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83375), [#83386](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83386), [#83264](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83264)
  - Suggested action: don't list every block. Explain that the options shown depend on the block, and give two or three examples.

- [ ] **[Filters Settings overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/filters-settings-overview/)**
  - "Supported blocks: Image, Cover, Gallery" is out of date. Duotone is now on Video ([#83979](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83979)), Media & Text ([#83981](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83981)) and the Gallery block itself, not only its images ([#83978](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83978)).
  - The page was last updated in 2023, so check all screenshots.

- [ ] **[Border & Shadow Settings overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/border-settings-overview/)**
  - The panel is now always called **Borders**, the **Border** and **Shadow** labels always show, and the unlink button moved up to the label row ([#82163](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82163), six screenshots in the PR).
  - Shadow is now on about 60 more blocks (for example Paragraph, Heading, Buttons, Gallery and Video). Border is new on Comments Pagination, Pagination, Home Link, Latest Comments, Tabs, Tab Panel, Post Navigation Link and Query No Results, and border style on Post Featured Image and Read More.
  - Suggested action: replace any "supported blocks" list with a short statement that most blocks now support shadow.

- [ ] **[Dimension Settings overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/dimension-controls-overview/)**
  - **Minimum height** lists only Cover, Content and Group. Minimum width and height are now on about 40 blocks (for example Buttons, Columns, Heading, Gallery, File and Media & Text).
  - **Block spacing:** Group can now set separate horizontal and vertical gaps, but only with the **Row**, **Stack** or **Grid** layout ([#81476](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81476)).
  - Padding is new on Embed ([#83963](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83963)) and Search ([#83984](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83984)), and padding, margin and block spacing on Pagination and Comments Pagination ([#83743](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83743), [#83744](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83744)).
  - The "Blocks that have dimension settings" list is out of date. Consider removing it rather than extending it. The page was last updated in 2023, so check all screenshots. See also #823 and #1666.

- [ ] **[Background Settings overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/background-settings-overview/)**
  - Background image, size and gradient are now on many more blocks (for example Heading, Buttons, Columns, Details, File and Site Title). Some blocks get gradient only.
  - **New:** you can set a background image from a URL, not only from the Media Library ([#82230](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82230), one recording in the PR).

**Source:** [WordPress 7.2 Source of Truth: Responsive styles and states, round two](https://wordpress-source-of-truth.space.fast/7-2/#responsive-styles) (Priority item)
**Tracking issue:** [Responsive style states for blocks - 7.2 tasks (gutenberg#80388)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/80388). Closed at Beta 1. Later work is tracked in [gutenberg#85243](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/85243) for 7.3.
**Planning issue:** #2567 (Block and site editor > Responsive styles, and Design tools > Layout and Position settings)
**7.1 issue for this article:** #2459

## Pages to update

- [ ] **[Responsive styles](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/responsive-styles/)**: the main update (details below).
- [ ] **[Position settings overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/position-settings-overview/)**: add that position can be set per viewport. This page was last updated in June 2024, so check the rest of it against 7.2 too.
- [ ] **[Styles overview](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/styles-overview/)**: the **Per-block CSS** section (state-specific custom CSS) and the Navigation Link states in **Blocks**. The Global Styles issue for 7.2 also touches this page, so coordinate the edits.
- [ ] **[Gallery block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/gallery-block/)**: columns, crop and aspect ratio per viewport. Gallery has several other 7.2 changes on #2567 (Order by, Grid variation, Duotone, Detach). If a separate Gallery block issue covers the article, add the responsive settings there and tick this box with a link to it.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** WordPress 7.1 introduced Tablet and Mobile styles. In 7.2, more settings can change by screen size: a block's position, custom CSS and the Gallery block's columns, crop and aspect ratio. The editor footer now shows which viewport you're editing and whether responsive styles are on, and Navigation Link blocks get hover, focus and active controls in Styles.

- [ ] **Position per viewport.** You can set a different position (for example, sticky) for Tablet and Mobile. In core, the Group block is the only block with position settings.
  [Enable setting position within viewport states (#83094)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83094), core ticket [Trac #66166](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/66166)
  *Sections affected:* **Limitations** in Responsive styles (which lists the settings that can vary by screen size) and the Position settings overview.

- [ ] **Custom CSS per state.** Custom CSS for a single block can be set for Tablet, Mobile and interactive states such as hover. Custom CSS set in Styles for a viewport now shows in the editor, and the inherited CSS shown in the Styles panels matches the selected viewport.
  [Enable style state-specific custom CSS (#83539)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83539)
  *Suggested action:* a short section in Responsive styles, and a note in **Applying Custom CSS > Per-block CSS** in the Styles overview.

- [ ] **Gallery columns, crop and aspect ratio per viewport.** The Gallery block's **Columns**, **Crop images to fit** and **Aspect ratio** settings can be different on Tablet and Mobile. Works with both the default and Grid gallery layouts.
  [Enable Gallery columns and crop controls in viewport states (#82003)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82003), [Enable viewport state values for Gallery aspect ratio (#82233)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82233)
  *Sections affected:* **Limitations** in Responsive styles, and **Block settings > Settings tab** in the Gallery block article.

- [ ] **Footer shows the viewport and responsive styles status.** The editor footer shows the selected viewport and whether **Responsive styles** is on. On the Desktop viewport, the option to turn on responsive styles isn't available.
  [Style states: Add footer viewport and responsive styles status (#84146)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/84146)
  *Sections affected:* **Setting responsive styles for a single block** (add how to tell responsive styles are on).

- [ ] **Clearer state badges in the block settings.** When a state is active, the state badges replace the block description in the **Settings** sidebar, and the badge has a tooltip. The device icon in the toolbar changes color while responsive styles are on.
  [Style states: Improve block inspector UI (#82649)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82649)
  *Sections affected:* the paragraph about the badge in **Setting responsive styles for a single block**, and its screenshot.

- [ ] **Navigation Link hover, focus and active states in Styles.** In **Styles > Blocks > Navigation Link**, you can now style the hover, focus, focus-visible and active states, so menu links can change on hover across the site.
  [Global Styles: Add pseudo-state controls for Navigation Link (#83451)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83451)
  *Note:* this overlaps with the Global Styles changes. Document it here. The Global Styles issue points to this one.

- [ ] **Inherited values shown in block settings.** Block settings now show the values a block inherits from Styles: as a placeholder or preselected option, with a dotted underline on the setting's label. A value set on the block itself overrides the inherited one.
  [Block Editor: Reflect inherited Global Styles values in block inspector controls (#77894)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/77894)
  *Suggested action:* a short note in **How responsive styles work** (inherited values also apply per viewport). This change affects all block settings, so it may also belong in the Global Styles issue.

### Check on the RC build before writing

- [ ] Steps in **Setting responsive styles for a block type**: the Styles panel opened from the editor toolbar now uses the editor's viewport dropdown to switch states, while the Styles panel opened from the Site Editor's main menu still uses the **States** dropdown. Check that both sets of steps still work.
- [ ] Footer status (#84146): confirm it shipped, what it says, and whether it hides when the footer is hidden in **Preferences**.
- [ ] Gallery: confirm the exact labels of the three settings and that they show a Tablet or Mobile badge.
- [ ] Position: confirm the sticky option behaves per viewport on the front end, not only in the editor.
- [ ] Inherited values (#77894): confirm the dotted underline and how it looks for color, spacing and typography.

### Not in 7.2, don't document

- Custom viewports or breakpoints added by plugins.
- Responsive values for block toolbar controls. The **Limitations** section is still correct that toolbar controls apply to every screen size.
- The developer API for custom responsive controls (`getStyleForState()`, `setStyleForState()`, the `styleStates` inspector slot). That's for the Field Guide, not HelpHub.
- Anything listed on [gutenberg#85243](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/85243) (the 7.3 iteration).

## Screenshots and media

- **Needed:** the editor footer with the viewport and responsive styles status, the Settings sidebar with a Tablet or Mobile badge (replacing the current screenshot), a Group block's **Position** setting with a Tablet badge, and the Gallery block settings on Mobile.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** Global Styles can now style form elements and citations. Elements such as links, buttons, headings and form controls are listed alongside blocks in **Styles > Blocks**, and their screens preview the state you're styling, such as hover. You can create your own duotone palettes in a new **Duotone** tab, and filter the block list to show only the blocks you've customized.

- [ ] **Citations, inputs and selects get typography and color controls.** **Styles > Typography > Elements** and the color elements list now include **Citations**, **Inputs** and **Selects**, alongside the existing text, links, headings and buttons. This lets search, comment and plugin forms match the rest of the site without custom CSS.
  [Global Styles: Expose additional elements in Typography and Colors (#80852)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/80852), core ticket [Trac #65880: Add pseudo-selector support for text inputs](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/65880)
  *Sections affected:* **Typography** (the elements list), **Colors > Customize the color of elements**.

- [ ] **Elements are listed alongside blocks.** **Styles > Blocks** now lists elements next to blocks, grouped under **Elements**, **Headings** and **Form controls**. Each element gets background, dimensions, border, shadow and custom CSS controls, and links and buttons get state controls, such as hover.
  [Global Styles: List elements alongside blocks (#81645)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81645)
  *Sections affected:* **Blocks** (and its subsections), **Applying Custom CSS > Per-block CSS** if it describes where custom CSS lives.

- [ ] **Element screens preview the selected state.** When you choose a state such as **Hover** on the **Link** or **Button** element screen, the preview now shows that state.
  [Global Styles: Preview the selected state on element screens (#83787)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83787)
  *Suggested action:* one or two sentences plus a screenshot in the new elements content.

- [ ] **Customized filter in Styles > Blocks.** A filter menu narrows the block list to only the blocks you've customized. Note: the dot that marked customized blocks was removed before release (#84657), so only the filter shipped. The #2567 checklist still mentions the dot.
  [Global Styles: filter and indicate blocks that have custom styles (#81373)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81373), [Global Styles: Remove the custom styles dot from the block list (#84657)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/84657)
  *Sections affected:* **Blocks**, and possibly **Reset your changes** (the filter helps find what to reset).

- [ ] **Custom duotone palettes.** **Styles > Colors > Edit palette** now has a **Duotone** tab next to **Color** and **Gradient**, so you can edit the theme's duotones and add your own. Before 7.2, duotones only appeared as a read-only grid in the **Gradient** tab.
  [Global Styles: Allow editing duotone palettes (#81605)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81605)
  *Sections affected:* Styles overview **Colors** (next to **Customize the theme gradients** and **Add custom gradient**), Colors settings overview **Duotone filter**, Filters settings overview **Adding to Global Styles**.

- [ ] **Label styling (theme builders only).** Themes can style `<label>` elements through `theme.json`. There's no UI for this, so at most add a short note for theme builders, or leave it to the developer docs.
  [Global styles: Register `<label>` as element (#81160)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81160)

- [ ] **Version details.** Add a changelog entry to each updated page.

- [ ] Optional: **[Work with blocks](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/work-with-blocks/)**: its block toolbar section doesn't mention notes. Consider one line about the **Add note** button.

## Update for 7.2

**Summary:** Notes move out of an invisible sidebar into a margin beside the editor canvas. A new **Notes** submenu lets you expand, minimize or hide them. Notes get emoji reactions, an **Add note** button in the block toolbar replaces the avatar indicator, highlights are clearer, and deleting a note can be undone.

- [ ] **Notes sit in a margin beside the canvas.** Notes now appear next to the content they refer to, scroll with the canvas, and stay open while the **Settings** sidebar is open.   *Sections affected:* the intro, **Add a note**, **Add multiple note threads to a block** and **Add a note to selected text** (all say notes appear "in the sidebar"), and **View notes for a block**.

- [ ] **New Notes submenu: Expand notes, Minimize notes, Hide notes.** Found in **Options > View > Notes**. Hiding notes is remembered.
  [Notes: Add show and hide options for floating notes (#83768)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83768)
  *Suggested action:* add a short section, for example "Show, minimize or hide notes", and link to the WordPress Block Editor article for the rest of the Options menu.

- [ ] **"Add note" button in the block toolbar.** Once a post has a note, the block toolbar shows an **Add note** button before **Options**. On a block that already has notes, the button shows the number of notes. It replaces the avatars that used to show in the toolbar.
  [Notes: Make the "Add note" toolbar button add-only and drop the avatars (#84635)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/84635)
  *Sections affected:* **Add a note** and **Add multiple note threads to a block** (add the toolbar button as a second way to add a note), and **View notes for a block** (it currently says the block toolbar shows the user's avatar, which is no longer true).

- [ ] **Emoji reactions.** You can react to a note with one of seven emoji (👍 ➕ ❤️ 🎉 😄 👀 🚀) instead of writing a reply.
  [Add emoji reactions to notes (#76767)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/76767), [Notes: Add thumbs up and plus reactions (#85565)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/85565), core ticket [Trac #64638](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/64638)
  *Suggested action:* add a section, for example "React to a note". Add a tip about using reactions to acknowledge feedback.

- [ ] **Clearer highlights.** Selecting a note keeps the block outline without dimming the rest of the content, block-level notes highlight the whole text block, and inline notes use a steadier tint with an underline.
  [Improve how notes highlight and connect to content (#80578)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/80578)
  *Sections affected:* **Add a note to selected text (inline notes)**. Likely a screenshot update only.

- [ ] **Undo after deleting a note.** The "Note deleted." notification now has an **Undo** action.
  [Notes: Add Undo to deleted note snackbar (#83988)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83988)
  *Sections affected:* **Edit or delete your note**.

- [ ] **Unsent notes are kept.** Text typed into a new note or reply is kept when you select another block or switch to the code editor.
  [Notes: Preserve unsent note and reply drafts (#84110)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/84110)
  *Suggested action:* one line in **Tips for effective collaboration** or the FAQ.

- [ ] **Inline notes on Accordion headings.** Selected text in an Accordion Heading now gets an inline note instead of a block-level note.
  [Accordion Heading: Anchor inline notes to selected title text (#84497)](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/84497)
  *Suggested action:* optional. Only needed if the article lists which blocks support inline notes.

- [ ] **Version details.** In **What you need**, mention that WordPress 7.2 added the canvas margin, reactions and the **Add note** button. Update the troubleshooting step "Open the Notes panel in the editor sidebar, or select a block and look for the Notes control in the toolbar" to match 7.2.

These details came from the PRs and the Source of Truth, and the UI may have changed since. Please confirm them on the latest 7.2 release candidate ([Playground](https://playground.wordpress.net/release)):

- [ ] Does the **Add note** toolbar button appear only once the post has at least one note, or on every block?

- [ ] Email to @mentioned users ([#79606](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/79606)) is listed on #2567 as a 7.2 change, but the Notes article already describes it. Confirm whether this shipped in 7.1 or 7.2, and whether anything about it changed.

### Not in 7.2, don't document

Per the tracking issue, these were moved to 7.3 or are still in progress: suggestion mode, search and filters in the **All notes** sidebar, an "unseen activity" dot, notes spanning multiple blocks, a full searchable emoji picker, and notes in templates.

title: New page: `WP_SECRETS_KEY` (WordPress 7.2)

labels.name: developer documentation (DevHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to developer documentation

labels.name: new document
labels.description: Requests for new page/article.

labels.name: needs discussion
labels.description: Issue that need discussion and team's decision. Will be discussed at the meeting.

body:
WordPress 7.2 adds the Secrets API ([#66187](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/66187)), which encrypts credentials that plugins store, such as API keys, under a key from a new `wp-config.php` constant, `WP_SECRETS_KEY`. Site Health will tell site owners to add this key, and we'd like to link it to a page that explains it ([#66380 comment:9](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/66380#comment:9)). This could be a HelpHub page, or a section on the wp-config.php page in the Advanced Administration Handbook, whichever fits better. It needs a stable URL.

What the page should cover:

- **What it is:** the key that encrypts secrets stored by WordPress and plugins. Without it, plugins can't use the Secrets API.
- **How to add it:** one line in `wp-config.php`, above "That's all, stop editing!", with a base64-encoded 32-byte random value. Site Health shows a ready-made line, and new installs get one automatically.
- **Back it up with your database:** a database backup without the key can't decrypt the secrets in it.
- **Never change it once secrets are stored.** Unlike the keys and salts, changing or removing it makes every stored secret unreadable until the old value is restored. Rotating the salts doesn't affect it.
- **Hosts** can define it for every site they run. A host or plugin that manages keys elsewhere, such as a key management service, may not need it at all. Site Health says so.
- **Multisite:** one key in `wp-config.php` covers the whole network.

The technical background and a full reference are at https://secretsapi.dev/. I'm happy to review a draft or write the first one.

title: [Advanced Admin] New page: Recovering a compromised WordPress site

labels.name: advanced administration
labels.description: Issues for Advanced administration Handbook

body:
## What is the new page you are requesting?

A page in the Advanced Administration Handbook, under Security, on responding to a known or suspected compromise. It would cover what an administrator or host does after a breach, for example:

- Confirming the compromise and preserving evidence (logs, a copy of the files and database) before cleaning up.
- Restoring from a known-good backup versus cleaning in place.
- Replacing WordPress core, plugins and themes with clean copies (for example with `wp core verify-checksums` and `wp plugin verify-checksums`).
- Checking for unknown administrator accounts, unexpected must-use plugins, and modified `wp-config.php` or `.htaccess` files.
- Rotating credentials: WordPress passwords, application passwords, the salts in `wp-config.php`, database, SFTP and hosting accounts.
- Getting blocklist warnings removed after cleanup.
- When to involve the hosting provider.

The end-user side could then shrink to a short, non-technical page: signs that a site may be hacked, who to contact, and a link to this handbook page.

## How will this new page help you?

There is no current guidance to link to when a site is compromised. I ran into this while working on the password reset docs (#1707, #79). The natural last step after a password reset is "if the account was compromised, a new password is not enough". But there is nowhere good to send the reader:

- The Advanced Administration Handbook has no page on breach response. [Hardening WordPress](https://developer.wordpress.org/advanced-administration/security/hardening/) covers prevention, not recovery.
- [FAQ My site was hacked](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/faq-my-site-was-hacked/) in the end-user docs is mostly links to external blog posts from 2008 to 2013. Several are on plain `http://` URLs, and it recommends specific vendors and services. #369 already noted that most of these links do not meet the [external linking policy](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/handbook/documentation-team-handbook/external-linking-policy/). Recent fixes (#1963) only patched a single broken link.

This page is also listed in #426 (FAQ content review: keep, move to DevHub, or delete). This issue proposes the "move" outcome for the technical part, with a page written from scratch rather than migrated as-is.

title: Enqueuing: AJAX handler examples call sanitize_post_title(), which does not exist

labels.name: developer documentation (DevHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to developer documentation

labels.name: plugins
labels.description: Issues for Plugin Developer Handbook

body:
## Issue Description
The AJAX handler examples call `sanitize_post_title( $title )` before saving the value with `update_user_meta()`. WordPress has no function named `sanitize_post_title()`, so the copied code ends with `Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined function sanitize_post_title()` when the AJAX request runs.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/javascript/enqueuing/

## Section of Page with the issue
- https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/javascript/enqueuing/#data (the `update_user_meta()` snippet)
- https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/javascript/enqueuing/#ajax-handler-summary (both complete handlers, `my_ajax_handler__json()` and `my_ajax_handler()`)

## Why is this a problem?
Developers copy these handlers directly. The handler fatals on the first request, so the example never works. The function is not defined anywhere in core (`grep -rn sanitize_post_title src/` in wordpress-develop returns nothing).

## Suggested Fix
`sanitize_post_title( $title )` → `sanitize_text_field( $title )` in all three places. [`sanitize_text_field()`](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/sanitize_text_field/) is the core function for a plain text value from user input (`wp-includes/formatting.php`).

I have a PR ready for developer-plugins-handbook.

title: Sub-Menus: outdated add_submenu_page() signature and a wrong add_options_page() parent slug

labels.name: developer documentation (DevHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to developer documentation

labels.name: plugins
labels.description: Issues for Plugin Developer Handbook

body:
## Issue Description
The **Add a Sub-Menu** section shows an old signature for `add_submenu_page()`. It ends with `callable $function = ''`. The current core signature is:

`add_submenu_page( $parent_slug, $page_title, $menu_title, $capability, $menu_slug, $callback = '', $position = null )`

The callback parameter is named `$callback`, and `$position` was added in WordPress 5.3 (`@since 5.3.0 Added the $position parameter.` in `wp-admin/includes/plugin.php`).

The **Predefined Sub-Menus** list also has two errors:
- `add_options_page()` is listed twice, once with `options-general.php` and once with `settings.php`. `add_options_page()` always uses `options-general.php`. `settings.php` is the Network Admin parent, which already has its own line at the end of the list.
- In the page source, the `add_users_page()` link starts with `hhttps://` instead of `https://`. The rendered page on developer.wordpress.org shows a working link, but the Markdown source is wrong.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/administration-menus/sub-menus/

## Section of Page with the issue
- https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/administration-menus/sub-menus/#add-a-sub-menu (signature)
- https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/administration-menus/sub-menus/#predefined-sub-menus (helper function list)

## Why is this a problem?
Developers do not learn about `$position` from this page, and the parameter name does not match the function reference. The duplicate `add_options_page()` line tells them the helper adds a page under `settings.php`, which it never does.

## Suggested Fix
- Signature: `callable $function = ''` → `callable $callback = '',` followed by `int|float $position = null`
- Remove the `add_options_page()` – `settings.php` line
- `hhttps://` → `https://` in the `add_users_page()` link

title: [Plugin handbook] How to Internationalize Your Plugin: explain WordPress 6.7 translation loading and JS translations

labels.name: developer documentation (DevHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to developer documentation

labels.name: plugins
labels.description: Issues for Plugin Developer Handbook

body:
## Issue Description

The "How to Internationalize Your Plugin" page doesn't mention the translation loading changes in WordPress 6.7. Since 6.7, translating a plugin's strings before the `init` action shows a "Translation loading for the … domain was triggered too early" notice, and `load_plugin_textdomain()` only registers the translation path instead of loading the file. The page's only loading example uses `init`, but it doesn't say why, or what goes wrong otherwise.

The "Handling JavaScript files" section only links to other pages and spells Gutenberg as "Gutenburg".

## URL of the Page with the Issue

https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/internationalization/how-to-internationalize-your-plugin/

## Section of Page with the issue

"Loading Text Domain" and "Handling JavaScript files".

## Why is this a problem?

Many plugins started showing the "too early" notice after 6.7. It usually only shows when a translation for the current language is installed, so it's easy to miss on an English test site. The explanation is only in the 6.7 dev note: https://make.wordpress.org/core/2024/10/21/i18n-improvements-6-7/

For JavaScript, a plugin that uses `wp.i18n` without calling `wp_set_script_translations()` never loads its JS translations, and the page doesn't name the function.

## Suggested Fix

Under "Loading Text Domain", add a short note: since 6.7 `load_plugin_textdomain()` only registers the path, and strings must not be translated before `init` (main plugin file, `plugins_loaded`, class constructors), with a link to the dev note.

Under "Handling JavaScript files", fix "Gutenburg" and add one sentence with the steps: `wp.i18n.__()` with the text domain, and `wp_set_script_translations()` after registering the script.

I'm happy to open the PR in developer-plugins-handbook.

title: [DevHub] Update wp_verify_nonce example to unslash and sanitize input

labels.name: developer documentation (DevHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to developer documentation

labels.name: [Status] Review
labels.description: Issue in review

body:
## Issue Description
The documentation example for `wp_verify_nonce()` shows a nonce value being read directly from `$_POST`. Since `$_POST` contains user-supplied data, the example should follow WordPress coding standards and security recommendations by **unslashing** and **sanitizing** the value before using it.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
[https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/)

## Section of Page with the issue
[Verifying a nonce passed in an AJAX request](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/#verifying-a-nonce-passed-in-an-ajax-request)

## Why is this a problem?
The example code that demonstrates nonce verification accesses `$_POST['my_nonce']` directly:

`wp_verify_nonce( $_POST['my_nonce'], 'process-comment' . $comment_id );`

This does not follow current WordPress coding standards and security recommendations, which advise sanitizing and unslashing user input before use.
Developers often copy examples from the documentation verbatim, so showing direct access to $_POST may unintentionally encourage unsafe patterns.

## Suggested Fix
Sanitizing and unslashing user input before use. 
Suggested update:

`wp_verify_nonce( sanitize_text_field( wp_unslash( $_POST['my_nonce'] ) ), 'process-comment' . $comment_id );`

## Issue Description
The Header Requirements page of the Plugin Handbook has several small grammar and punctuation errors, mostly in the opening sentence and the Header Fields list.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/plugin-basics/header-requirements/

## Section of Page with the issue
The introductory paragraph, the Header Fields list (Plugin URI, Description, Network and Update URI), and the sentence introducing the second code example.

## Why is this a problem?
The opening sentence is ungrammatical ("should include header comment what tells WordPress that a file is a plugin"). It is the first thing readers see on the page, and it is also used as the page's meta description, so it shows up in search results and link previews. The other items are smaller inconsistencies and redundancies that make the text harder to read.

## Suggested Fix
**1. Introductory paragraph** (missing article, "what" instead of "that", "a file" instead of "the file")
Current: the main PHP file should include header comment what tells WordPress that a file is a plugin and provides information about the plugin.
Suggested: the main PHP file should include a header comment that tells WordPress that the file is a plugin and provides information about the plugin.

**2. Plugin URI** (says the URL "should be" unique, then that it "must be" unique)
Current: The home page of the plugin, which should be a unique URL, preferably on your own website. This *must be unique* to your plugin. You cannot use a WordPress.org URL here.
Suggested: The home page of the plugin, preferably on your own website. This *must be unique* to your plugin. You cannot use a WordPress.org URL here.

**3. Description** (the same admin screen is called the "Plugins list" in the Plugin Name field)
Current: as displayed in the Plugins section in the WordPress Admin.
Suggested: as displayed in the Plugins list in the WordPress Admin.

**4. Network** (unnecessary comma: both verbs share the same subject)
Current: Can only be set to *true*, and should be left out when not needed.
Suggested: Can only be set to *true* and should be left out when not needed.

**5. Update URI** (missing article; the Requires Plugins field already says "read the related dev note")

title: [DevHub] WP_Query::get_posts use case clarification

labels.name: developer documentation (DevHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to developer documentation

body:
<!--
Please fill out the following sections with as many details as you can.
We can't work on fixing an issue unless we have all the details. 
So please be sure your submission is complete; if it's not, it will be marked as incomplete, and closed without being fixed.

-->

## Issue Description

I've encountered a pretty gnarly issue a few times with my (incorrect) usage of `WP_Query::get_posts()` which can be quite tricky to debug.

Essentially, `new WP_Query($args)->get_posts()` can silently corrupt `tax_query` results due to core code that writes the first taxonomy and term to `query_vars['taxonomy']` and `query_vars['term']` which then effects the SQL generated when `WP_Query::get_posts()` runs the query for the second time.

This causes incorrect results particularly when you're trying to do a `tax_query` with multiple taxonomies and term arrays with `'relation' => 'AND'` and `'operator' => 'IN'` - (for example, if you're using `wp_query` to build faceted search interfaces). The first taxonomy and term end up appended as a new separate clause with a single term, even if that taxonomy had multiple terms in the originally passed arguments.

I don't really think this is a bug, its more an issue of me not realising that `WP_Query::get_posts()` should only ever be used internally and *should never* be used to get results from the already constructed `WP_Query` object.

The documentation page for `WP_Query::get_posts()` is usually going to be the first result if you google something like "get posts from a wp_query", the method name can be easily misconstrued as a simple getter, and the documentation is minimal.

## URL of the Page with the Issue

[https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/classes/wp_query/get_posts/](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/classes/wp_query/get_posts/)

## Section of Page with the issue

Description

## Why is this a problem?

Its perfectly reasonable for a developer to end up on this documentation page when looking up how to get the _results_ from an already constructed WP_Query and incorrectly assume that this method is what they want. In lots of cases, this would lead to that developer using `->get_posts()` instead of `->posts`. This will often be missed, since get_posts will re-run the query and often produce the same results, however it is inefficient because they would essentially be running the query twice, and it can produce unexpected silent failures in complex tax_queries as described above in the Issue Description.

## Suggested Fix

I think the fix is a one line documentation change:

"Note: This method is used internally by WP_Query and should not be used to retrieve post results from an already instantiated WP_Query object. To get the array of post results from a WP_Query, you should use `->posts` instead"

body:
This issue was originally created as [HelpHub #333](https://github.com/WordPress/HelpHub/issues/333) by atachibana and comment was added by [ashfame](https://github.com/ashfame).

---
There are two methods:
1. Using the plugin
2. Setting up WordPress manually (without plugin)

For above method 2, the step will be (but might be missing)
1. Backup WordPress files and database
2. Set SSL certificate
3. Change WordPress URL from Administration Screen
4. Replace the string 'http' to 'https' in the database contents
5. Add redirect code into .htaccess

---
## Comment by [ashfame](https://github.com/ashfame)

I just switched an old site to refresh up my memory for the exact steps:

#### Actual Instructions

- Take a backup of files and database in case you need to revert for whatever reasons.
- Get your webhost to install a TLS (also referred to as SSL) certificate for your website
- Once installed ensure that your website is accessible on `https` URL, by simply replacing `http` with `https` i.e. adding a `s` to it. Eg: If your website was `http://www.domain.com`, new URL would be `https://www.domain.com`
- See if you have any errors in your browser console complaining about mixed content, as you browse different pages on your website. Usually when using good quality plugin and theme, there won't be an issue. But if you do, you will need to resolve these issues.
- Once you are satisfied with the results and are ready to flip the switch, go ahead and update the website URL in WordPress admin: `Settings` > `General`.
- Now if you try to access http version of your website you will be redirected to https version. Best to try in an incognito/private window in your browser to test this.

#### Potential issues:

> `http` to `https` redirect isn't working

I am not sure if changing the URL in WordPress causes it to issue redirects, though I believe it does. I never use it, as I always handle redirects on a server level.

> Mixed-content warnings

Depending on what resources are causing these errors, it can either be your theme, any plugin you use or actual content you load in post/page and requires a different approach for each one of them.

Post/page content requires you to replace string, can be done via this plugin https://wordpress.org/plugins/better-search-replace/

Theme/plugins would require using the right functions to generate URLs or simply update the hardcoded urls to be https.

body:
<!--
Please fill out the following sections with as many details as you can.
We can't work on fixing an issue unless we have all the details. 
So please be sure your submission is complete; if it's not, it will be marked as incomplete, and closed without being fixed.

-->

## Issue Description
It is stated that "WordPress supports four border settings", but in fact it now supports a 5th setting - the new "[Border Radius Presets](https://make.wordpress.org/core/2025/11/12/theme-json-border-radius-presets-support-in-wordpress-6-9/)". This setting is not mentioned in the list of border settings.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
https://developer.wordpress.org/themes/global-settings-and-styles/settings/border/

## Section of Page with the issue
The paragraph immediately after the "Border settings" heading and the unordered bulleted list after it.

## Why is this a problem?
It is obvious!

## Suggested Fix
This is my proposal for reformulation of the hole heading and its content:

## Border settings
WordPress supports five border settings that you can configure via the `settings.border` property in `theme.json`. Each setting allows you to enable or disable a specific border feature. Four of them accept a boolean (`true` or `false`) value, while the fifth accepts a list of objects to define border radius presets.

- `color`: Enables/Disables the border-color picker.
- `radius`: Enables/Disables the border-radius control.
- `style`: Enables/Disables the border-style selector (users can choose `solid`, `dashed`, or `dotted`).
- `width`: Enables/Disables the border-width input.
- `radiusSizes`: Defines a curated set of border radius presets that users can select from in the Block Editor.

### Default configuration
By default, the first four border properties are set to false:
```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "settings": {
    "border": {
      "color": false,
      "radius": false,
      "style": false,
      "width": false
      "radiusSizes": []
    }
  }
}
```
### Border radius presets (`radiusSizes`)
You can define border radius presets in `theme.json` under `settings.border.radiusSizes`. These presets provide consistent design values while still allowing users to enter custom values. The property accepts an array of border radius objects, each with three required properties:

- `name`: The label for your border radius preset, which will be internationalized (so that it can be translated) and shown to the user in some contexts, such as tooltips.
- `slug`: A unique machine-readable slug/ID for your border radius preset. This is used to generate CSS custom properties and CSS classes.
- `size`: A valid CSS length value (e.g., px, %).

For example, to add `None`, `Small`, `Medium`, `Large` and `Full` border radius presets:
```json
{
  "version": 3,
  "settings": {
    "border": {
      "radiusSizes": [
        {
          "name": "None",
          "slug": "none",
          "size": "0"
        },
        {
          "name": "Small",
          "slug": "small",
          "size": "4px"
        },
        {
          "name": "Medium",
          "slug": "medium",
          "size": "8px"
        },
        {
          "name": "Large",
          "slug": "large",
          "size": "16px"
        },
        {
          "name": "Full",
          "slug": "full",
          "size": "9999px"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
- With 1–8 presets, users see a slider with stops for each preset.
- With 9 or more presets, the control displays as a dropdown select menu.
- Users can always access custom value input through the custom button to the right of the control.
- The interface automatically adapts based on the number of presets you define.

title: [HelpHub] Clarify theme ZIP file structure for updates

labels.name: user documentation (HelpHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to end-user documentation

body:
The current documentation (https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/work-with-themes/#adding-new-themes-using-the-administration-screens and https://learn.wordpress.org/lesson/updating-your-theme/) implicitly assumes that a theme's ZIP file will contain a single root folder and that all theme files will reside within that folder. This is a common and well-known best practice among experienced developers. However, it is not explicitly stated as a hard requirement (or I'm unable to find this requirement in the docs).

This lack of explicit documentation can lead to a specific bug, as demonstrated in the Trac ticket https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/63737. When a user attempts to update a theme via ZIP upload, if the theme's files are at the root of the ZIP archive (instead of being inside a containing folder), a previous failed update attempt (e.g., trying to upload the theme ZIP through the plugin installer) can cause subsequent, correct update attempts to fail. WordPress, in this scenario, creates a new directory (e.g., my-theme-1) instead of overwriting the existing theme folder, breaking the update process.

Proposed Change:
Add a new, clear, and prominent section to the relevant documentation that explicitly states the correct ZIP file structure for themes. This should be added to both developer-facing and user-facing documentation.
